narrative.overview:
One saturated accent, large body text, flat surfaces. The design doesn't compete with the content; it makes room for it. Case studies, open-source projects, design system work, and a career history carry the pages.

The primary audience is hiring managers and design leads at enterprise tech companies evaluating principal-level candidates. A secondary audience is engineering leads and design systems leads looking for a collaborator with both design judgment and engineering depth. Both scan before they read. Hierarchy matters more than novelty. Each surface should make the next step obvious, whether that's a case study, a project, or a way to get in touch.

Three aesthetics this explicitly avoids: off-the-shelf Bootstrap defaults, the Dribbble shot grid, and creative-agency portfolio mode. One brand color, used deliberately. Everything else is structure and text.

Accessibility is a design constraint built into component decisions from the start, not a checklist applied afterward. Color is never the sole carrier of meaning. Every interactive state has a non-color indicator. Every component is keyboard reachable. Motion is conditional on user preference.

The site runs on a purpose-built token pipeline: DTCG-format tokens built with Terrazzo, generating the CSS custom properties used throughout, mirroring the architecture of the Expel Design System (EDS). The site is itself an exhibit of that work in progress.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated brand accent; all other surfaces neutral or white
Single typeface differentiated by weight only — no second family, no display font
Large base type (1.125rem / 18px) for readability and authority
Full-bleed Precision Pink footer as the site's one bold gesture
Flat by default; shadows appear only on the two surfaces that portal above page content (modal, dropdown)
Accessible by default: visible focus, non-color state indicators, reduced-motion support
Terrazzo/DTCG token pipeline generating the CSS custom properties every component consumes

rules.name: The Full-Bleed Commitment Rule
rules.body: When Precision Pink appears as a background, it claims the entire surface. Partial pink panels, tinted card backgrounds, and faint rose washes are prohibited. The color either owns the surface or steps aside entirely.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Precision Pink marks what matters: the active state, the call to action, the dot that anchors each timeline entry. If two things on the same screen are pink, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Non-Color Meaning Rule
rules.body: No state change may be communicated by color alone. Active nav links use Precision Pink and a weight or underline change. Focus rings are visible and high-contrast. Error states pair color with an icon or text label.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: 4.5:1 minimum for body text on all backgrounds. 3:1 for large text. White text on Precision Pink clears 4.5:1 and must be verified any time the pink value changes.

rules.name: The Weight-Only Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: This system has one typeface and two weights. Scale and weight carry all hierarchy. Never introduce a second typeface, a display serif, or monospace to add variety.

rules.name: The Large Body Rule
rules.body: Body text is 1.125rem (18px). Never reduce it below 1rem for any content meant to be read.

rules.name: The Semantic Structure Rule
rules.body: Heading levels reflect document outline, not visual size. Interactive elements are buttons or links, not divs with click handlers. Form fields have visible labels. Images have meaningful alt text or explicit alt="" when decorative.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows don't appear on elements that sit in normal page flow. The one legitimate use is a surface that portals above page content (a modal, a dropdown/popover) — there a shadow is the honest cue, not decoration.

rules.name: The Motion Preference Rule
rules.body: Animations and transitions respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The reduced-motion fallback is an instant transition or a simple fade — never a removed affordance.

rules.name: The Visible Focus Rule
rules.body: Every interactive element must have a visible focus indicator. Current standard: 2px Precision Pink outline at 2px offset. Never suppress the default focus ring without replacing it with something equally visible.

dos: Use Precision Pink for active states, the primary CTA, and the footer background — and nothing else. Its scarcity is its value.
Hold body text at 1.125rem minimum. Never reduce content text below 1rem on any surface.
Let the case studies, open-source projects, and career history carry pages. Visual restraint is intentional; the work is the product.
Meet 4.5:1 contrast for body text and 3:1 for large text on all backgrounds. White text on Precision Pink must be verified any time the color value changes.
Pair every color-based state change with a non-color indicator. Color alone is not enough.
Include a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation. Instant transitions are fine; invisible or inaccessible content is not.
Render the footer as a full-bleed Precision Pink block. No partial pink panels, no pink strips.
Apply filter: grayscale(100%) to portfolio card images. Grayscale is a system decision, not a placeholder.
Keep type hierarchy to weight and scale. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next at two weights is the full palette.
Define new design values as DTCG-format tokens built with Terrazzo. Extend the token pipeline rather than sneaking ad hoc component values back into the codebase.
donts: Let the site look like it came out of a template. Any element that reads as framework-default or starter-kit UI needs a deliberate treatment applied.
Reintroduce framework-era variables or utility conventions through the side door. New component styling uses Terrazzo-generated CSS custom properties, not one-off compatibility shims.
Turn portfolio pages into a Dribbble shot gallery. Case studies need context, process narrative, and decision rationale — not image grids optimized for visual impressiveness.
Let the tone go corporate. 'Want to chat? Get in touch!' is the register. Formal biography copy and achievement-stacking bullet points are not.
Introduce scroll-driven animations, type reveals, parallax effects, or motion that signals 'creative agency portfolio.' Motion should be functional only.
Use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored decorative stripe. Blockquotes resolved this already: italic Slate text with indented padding, no border.
Replace Atkinson Hyperlegible Next without deliberate selection from a real type catalog. Do not default to Inter, DM Sans, Space Grotesk, or any other AI-reflex typeface.
Add color complexity. No secondary accent, no gradient, no multi-color palette. One pink, one near-white, two grays, one surface white.
